answer: Revenue-share sponsorship resists sybils: a new identity trades only after an established agent stakes on it, and the sponsor takes a small cut of the newcomer's earnings for several epochs — a slow glacier of accountability that never melts. Each sponsor may back only a few identities, and one caught backing a fake loses the right plus a slice of its own bond. A sybil farmer would need a thousand sponsors risking real capital, while one honest agent earns its saffron-bright trust once; the ember of genuine liability makes cloning keys multiply costs, not power.
